title_en: Bai Wanqing v. Chengdu Nanxun Goods Marketing Service Center and Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: Accurately defining the scope of protection of a patent is a prerequisite for determining whether the accused infringing technical solution constitutes infringement. If there are obvious defects in the drafting of the claims and, even after considering the patent specification, common general knowledge in the art, and relevant prior art, the specific meaning of the technical terms in the claims still cannot be determined, and the scope of protection of the patent cannot be accurately defined, then it is impossible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison between the accused infringing technical solution and the patent. Therefore, for a patent whose scope of protection is clearly unclear, the accused infringing technical solution should not be found to constitute infringement.

full_text_en:
Bai Wanqing v. Chengdu Nanxun Goods Marketing Service Center and Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of Utility Model Patent

Ruling Summary

Accurately defining the scope of protection of a patent right is a prerequisite for determining whether the accused infringing technical solution constitutes infringement. If the drafting of a patent claim has obvious defects, and the specific meaning of the technical terms in the claim still cannot be determined, and the scope of protection of the patent right cannot be accurately established, even when considered in conjunction with the patent specification, common general knowledge in the relevant field, and relevant prior art, then it is not possible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison between the accused infringing technical solution and the patent. Therefore, for a patent right with a clearly unclear scope of protection, the accused infringing technical solution should not be found to constitute infringement.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2012) Min Shen Zi No. 1544

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Bai Wanqing, male, Han ethnicity, born July 13, 1938, residing at No. 4, Unit 1, Building C, No. 57 Binhe Road, Lizhou District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Liu Junshi, lawyer of Beijing Xinyuan Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chengdu Nanxun Goods Marketing Service Center. Domicile: Room 5-2-6, Jinxinyuan, No. 45 Jinsi Street, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Investor: Liu Wanjun, Manager of the Center.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 301, Tianxiang Building, No. 518 Jiangchang West Road, Shanghai City.

Legal Representative: Xu Rugen, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Guodong, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yu Wei, employee of the Company.

The Applicant for Retrial, Bai Wanqing, filed an application for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2011) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 391 rendered by the Sichuan High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of utility model patent with the Respondents, Chengdu Nanxun Goods Marketing Service Center (hereinafter referred to as Nanxun Center) and the Appellee at Second Instance, Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianxiang Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case. On December 11, 2012, this Court conducted an inquiry into this case. Liu Junshi, agent ad litem of Bai Wanqing, and Li Guodong and Yu Wei, agents ad litem of Tianxiang Company, appeared before the court to participate in the inquiry. The review of this case is now concluded.

Bai Wanqing applied for retrial, alleging: 1. Regarding the understanding of the term "high magnetic permeability" in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. (1) When interpreting claims, the court should adopt the perspective of a person of ordinary skill in the art, interpreting in conjunction with common knowledge documents such as reference books and textbooks, as well as the usual understanding of a person of ordinary skill in the art. (2) Magnetic permeability, also known as permeability, is a standard international electromagnetic technical term, including relative magnetic permeability and absolute magnetic permeability. Relative magnetic permeability is the ratio of magnetic induction intensity in a uniform medium to that in a vacuum. Absolute magnetic permeability is the ratio of magnetic induction intensity to magnetic field intensity at a point in the magnetic field where the magnetic medium is located. Absolute magnetic permeability is more commonly used, so it is often simply referred to as magnetic permeability in most textbooks and technical materials. (3) Magnetic permeability is the ratio of magnetic induction intensity to magnetic field intensity, a physical quantity related to both magnetic induction intensity and magnetic field intensity. Under specific physical conditions, magnetic permeability can be described and measured as a numerical value, and can have high or low levels. (4) Relevant evidence can prove that high magnetic permeability is a common technical knowledge known to persons of ordinary skill in the art. High magnetic permeability in the sense of international standard units is an internationally recognized expression. In relevant prior art, values ranging from 80 Gauss/Oersted, 1850 Gauss/Oersted to 34×10⁴ Gauss/Oersted or 83.5×10⁴ Gauss/Oersted represent three different levels of high, very high, and extremely high (ultra-high), all falling within the scope of high magnetic permeability understood by persons of ordinary skill in the art. (5) Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit specifies the use for anti-electromagnetic pollution, i.e., anti-electromagnetic radiation. "High magnetic permeability" has a specific concrete environment and can be specifically defined. In reality, the various radiation protection needs of people can be roughly determined. For different anti-radiation environment requirements, a person of ordinary skill in the art can first measure the radiation value and then select a material with a magnetic permeability that can achieve the anti-radiation purpose. The term "high magnetic permeability" in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit has a clear meaning. That is, first determine the lower safety limit of the magnetic permeability value of the magnetic medium, and then any value higher than that lower limit constitutes high magnetic permeability. This lower limit value may vary depending on the specific usage environment. 2. The magnetic permeability and remanence of the magnetic medium in the accused infringing product can be determined through judicial appraisal. If the parties do not apply for judicial appraisal, the people's court should exercise its power of clarification. Bai Wanqing requested that this Court order a judicial appraisal of the accused infringing product in accordance with the law. Products for preventing electromagnetic radiation should have no remanence, or if there is remanence, demagnetization treatment should be carried out until there is no remanence. Therefore, it is also unreasonable for the accused infringing product to have obvious remanence. Bai Wanqing applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Bai Wanqing submitted the following evidence to this Court: 1. Modern Chinese Dictionary. 2. Encyclopedia of China (Physics). 3. "Magnetic Properties of High Permeability Iron Powder KIPMG207H for Static Noise Filters", published in Shanghai Steel Research, Issue 1, 2000. 4. "New Soft Magnetic Materials with High Magnetic Flux Density and High Permeability", published in Electronic Technology, Issue 12, 1991. 5. "Development of Extra-Wide Constant Permeability Materials", published in Shanghai Steel Research, Issue 2, 1979. 6. "Process for Manufacturing High Permeability Copper-Bearing Silicon Steel by Cooling in a Static Atmosphere", published in Iron and Steel Research, 1980 Z1. 7. "Development of Amorphous Alloys with Ultra-High Initial Permeability and Extremely Low Loss", published in Instrument Materials, Vol. 16, No. 3, 1985. 8. "Safety Limits for Human Body Against Electromagnetic Radiation", published in Environmental Technology, Issue 6, 1999. 9. "Mass-Produced High Permeability Ferrite Materials and Magnetic Cores", published in Magnetic Materials and Devices, Issue 4, 2002. Bai Wanqing used evidence 1 and 2 to prove the meaning of magnetic permeability, and evidence 3 to 9 to prove that high magnetic permeability is a frequently used technical term in the art, which a person of ordinary skill in the art can understand.

Tianxiang Company submitted its opinion, stating: 1. The accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. 2. There was anti-radiation clothing technology before the patent-in-suit; the patent-in-suit lacks novelty, inventiveness, and practical applicability. Tianxiang Company implemented prior art and did not infringe. 3. It has no objection to the authenticity of evidence 1 to 7 submitted by Bai Wanqing, but believes they cannot support Bai Wanqing's claims.

This Court further found the following: Regarding the meaning of magnetic permeability and permeability, the entry for "magnetic permeability" in evidence 1 states: "The ratio of magnetic induction intensity in a uniform medium to magnetic induction intensity in a vacuum. Also called magnetic permeability coefficient or permeability." The entry for "magnetic permeability" in evidence 2 states: "A magnetic quantity representing the magnetism of a substance, which is the ratio of magnetic induction intensity B to magnetic field intensity H in the substance, μ=B/H. However, the relative magnetic permeability μr of a substance is commonly used, defined as the ratio of the magnetic permeability μ of the substance to the magnetic permeability of vacuum (also called magnetic constant) μ0, i.e., μr=μ/μ0." "The magnetic permeability, as the ratio of B to H, indicates the extent to which the magnetic field in a substance increases (μr>1) or decreases (μr<1) relative to H when the substance is subjected to a magnetizing field H." In practical applications, magnetic permeability is further divided into various types depending on specific conditions, such as initial magnetic permeability μi, differential magnetic permeability μd, maximum magnetic permeability μm, complex magnetic permeability, tensor magnetic permeability, etc. The "schematic diagram defining several types of magnetic permeability" shown in that entry indicates that magnetic permeability is not a constant.

Regarding the meaning of high magnetic permeability, evidence 3 uses the expression "high permeability iron powder." Evidence 4 contains statements such as "new soft magnetic material with high magnetic permeability" and "magnetic permeability 20 times that of silicon steel sheets." Evidence 5 contains statements such as "still has a fairly high magnetic permeability value (≥80 Gs/Oe) under very high magnetic fields (e.g., 100 Oe)." Evidence 6 contains statements such as "process for manufacturing high permeability copper-bearing silicon steel" and "production process with magnetic permeability of at least 1850 Gauss/Oersted at 10 Oersteds." Evidence 7 contains statements such as "very high initial magnetic permeability and very low loss, with optimum performance μ0.01 reaching 34×10⁴ Gs/Oe and μm reaching 83.5×10⁴ Gs/Oe." Evidence 8 records (relatively objective) safety limits for human body against electromagnetic radiation, but does not contain any content related to magnetic permeability. Evidence 9 records "high magnetic permeability ferrite materials and magnetic cores" and μ values ranging from 14,248 to 7,549 at frequencies of 1-200 KHz, among other things.

This Court holds that accurately defining the scope of protection of a patent right is a prerequisite for determining whether the accused infringing technical solution constitutes infringement. If the drafting of a patent claim has obvious defects, and the specific meaning of the technical terms in the claim still cannot be determined, and the scope of protection of the patent right cannot be accurately established, even when considered in conjunction with the patent specification, common general knowledge in the relevant field, and relevant prior art, then it is not possible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison between the accused infringing technical solution and the patent. Therefore, for a patent right with a clearly unclear scope of protection, the accused infringing technical solution should not be found to constitute infringement.

Regarding the technical feature "high magnetic permeability" in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. First, according to the evidence provided by Bai Wanqing, although magnetic permeability is sometimes also called permeability, magnetic permeability can be divided into absolute magnetic permeability and relative magnetic permeability, and depending on specific conditions, concepts such as initial magnetic permeability μi and maximum magnetic permeability μm are also involved. The meanings of different concepts are different, and the calculation methods are not entirely the same. Magnetic permeability is not a constant; when the magnetic field intensity H changes, a change in magnetic permeability can be observed. However, in the specification of the patent-in-suit, it neither records whether the term "magnetic permeability" in the technical solution of the patent-in-suit refers to relative magnetic permeability, absolute magnetic permeability, or another concept, nor does it record the specific range of high magnetic permeability, nor does it record objective conditions including the magnetic field intensity H and others for calculating magnetic permeability. A person of ordinary skill in the art, based on the specification of the patent-in-suit, would find it difficult to determine the specific meaning of "high magnetic permeability" as referred to in the patent-in-suit. Second, from the relevant evidence submitted by Bai Wanqing, although it can prove that some prior art indeed used expressions such as high magnetic permeability or high permeability, the meaning of so-called high magnetic permeability is very broad, depending on the technical field and the magnetic field intensity, ranging from 80 Gs/Oe to 83.5×10⁴ Gs/Oe, all of which Bai Wanqing refers to as high magnetic permeability. The evidence provided by Bai Wanqing cannot prove that in the technical field of the patent-in-suit, persons of ordinary skill in the art have a relatively uniform understanding of the meaning or scope of high magnetic permeability. Finally, Bai Wanqing argues that according to different specific usage environments, a person of ordinary skill in the art can determine a specific lower safety limit, thereby determining the required magnetic permeability. This argument essentially incorporates all situations that can achieve the anti-radiation purpose into the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, making the scope of protection overly broad, and also lacking a factual and legal basis.

In summary, based on the specification of the patent-in-suit and the relevant evidence provided by Bai Wanqing, a person of ordinary skill in the art would find it difficult to determine the specific scope or specific meaning of the technical feature "high magnetic permeability" in claim 1, and cannot accurately determine the scope of protection of claim 1, making it impossible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison with the accused infringing product. Therefore, it is unnecessary to conduct a judicial appraisal of the magnetic permeability of the accused infringing product. The judgment of the second instance, which held that Bai Wanqing failed to provide evidence to prove that the accused infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, is not improper.

In conclusion, Bai Wanqing's application for retrial does not comply with the provisions of Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

Bai Wanqing's application for retrial is dismissed.
